# Independent audit of interval half-depth rigidity and extraction

Audited independently by the depth/Helly route:

    candidate f9fd3b8e5ea799fa
    supporting computation verify_interval_reflection_variation_identity.py

Result: PASS. The exact variation identity, rigidity, finite-fiber
stability, and all-threshold extraction equivalence hold with the stated
scope. The supplied Fraction verifier passes. No correction was needed.

## 1. Through-point profiles and vertical boundary mass

For an actual point (j,c), each positive interval contributes a continuous
clipped affine function of slope a. All noncentral contributions become
constant at both finite tails; the own-fiber contribution is U_0. Thus
F is continuous, piecewise affine, and has exactly the stated endpoint
limits m_-+U_0 and m_++U_0. Missing intervals and zero-length point fibers
contribute zero throughout.

Every nonvertical boundary meets a positive interval fiber in at most
one point, so the opposite closed cap has mass M-F(a). A vertical through-
point cap includes the whole own fiber, and its mass is at least the
corresponding finite-slope plateau. Hence vertical caps cannot lower the
infimum. Shifting an arbitrary containing cap through the point only
decreases mass. This proves the exact absolute depth formula (3), even
when the center's own fiber has zero length or c is an interval endpoint.

## 2. Nested slope intervals and the exact reflection loss

Convexity with the actual anchor (j,c) proves both nesting inclusions,
including when a more distant fiber is missing or a point. Away from the
finite collection of interval endpoints, each side's active indices are
a prefix. Thus all nonzero differences between the plus and minus
indicators have one sign at a fixed slope. The equality

    abs(sum k(1_minus-1_plus))=sum k abs(1_minus-1_plus)

is therefore valid pointwise almost everywhere. It is not an application
of the generally false equality case of the triangle inequality for
arbitrary interval collections.

The signs of F' are correct: a right fiber's threshold increases at
speed k and loses length, while a left fiber's threshold decreases at
speed k and gains length. The scale factor k converts the symmetric
difference of the two slope intervals into the full two-fiber reflection
loss. The factor two in the retained intersection accounts for the two
reflected source fibers, whose intersection lengths agree by reflection.

For the own interval, its reflected overlap length is twice the smaller
distance from c to its endpoints. Its loss is exactly abs(2U_0-w_0),
including at either endpoint or at a zero-length interval. The endpoint
limits of F rewrite this as the claimed own-fiber imbalance. Since F is
continuous piecewise affine and constant at infinity, its total variation
is exactly the integral of abs(F'). Summing proves (8) with no jump terms
or omitted boundary mass.

## 3. Rigidity and quantitative stability

Depth M/2 is equivalent to F identically M/2 by (3). The variation identity
then gives R=M. Conversely R=M means the retained symmetric subset
exhausts the positive mixed measure. Reflection is an isometry, so the
whole measure is symmetric about the point. Every closed through-point
cap has at least half this mass; a nonvertical one has null boundary and
exactly half. This proves every implication in the stated equivalence.

The proof concerns symmetry of the positive-length MEASURE, as required.
Unmatched zero-length geometric fibers need not be reflected. Finiteness
and symmetry identify the true full ambient centroid with the center.

For the stability bound the anchor is expressly assumed to have positive
length. There are then at most 2(N-1) slope knots from noncentral positive
fibers, at most 2(N-1)-1 nonconstant intervening affine intervals, and
each endpoint-value change is at most 2delta. The own-fiber imbalance is
also at most 2delta. Their sum is at most 4(N-1)delta. For N=1, F is
constant and the exact loss is 2delta. The note does not incorrectly
apply the N-1 count at an anchor on a zero-length fiber.

## 4. All thresholds in the extraction equivalence

For every 0<t<=M, a locally half-deep convex subbody with true integer
centroid has a symmetric mixed measure by the proved rigidity. Its entire
positive measure is retained by reflecting the original source about
that centroid, so the original R is at least its mass.

Conversely E=C intersect (2y-C) is compact, convex, and symmetric. If it
has positive interval fibers at two different integer bases, the hull
of those intervals has nonempty two-dimensional interior. Therefore E
itself is a convex BODY, with the required mass, true centroid, and half
depth. No ambient interior of E is presumed before this check.

If E has only one positive integer fiber, symmetry forces its base to be
j. Its length is at most the full original K_j. Intersecting C with a
closed slab j-epsilon<=z<=j+epsilon, 0<epsilon<1/2, retains exactly this
full original integer fiber. The slab intersection is full dimensional:
the slab interior contains a point of K_j, and interior points of the
original convex body approach it. It has mixed mass |K_j|>=R(y)>=t and
its true centroid is the midpoint of that sole interval, with local depth
exactly one half. This new center is allowed by the existential statement.

Thus all threshold values, including t=M, are covered. The implication
does not discard positive vertical boundary fibers and does not need E
to be full dimensional in the one-fiber case. The special threshold M/2
is exactly equivalent to the stated half-mass reflection-retention
question; that universal retention assertion remains unproved here.

## 5. Exact verification

The supplied verifier passes its full rational grid of actual anchor
points, the displayed four-fiber examples, the prefix identity, and the
finite-N stability inequality. I separately checked the geometric knot
count, zero/missing-fiber cases, and full-dimensional slab argument; these
are not inferred from the finite numerical examples.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
